newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DUVAL TAKES THREE-SHOT LEAD AND SEVERAL RECORDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUVAL TAKES THREE-SHOT LEAD AND SEVERAL RECORDS.

text.p: David Duval claimed several records while taking a three-shot lead after three rounds of the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am Saturday.

In the celebrity-filled tournament played on three courses, Duval shot a 62 at Pebble Beach G.L., equalling the course record set by Tom Kite in 1982. Duval's front-nine score of 28 lowered that record by two strokes.

Duval's third-round lead of 18 under par was four strokes better than the previous best 54-hole total in the tournament. It was also one stroke better than Peter Jacobsen's record 72-hole winning score of 17 under in 1995.
Heading into the final round in second place were second-round leader Jim Furyk, who shot a 69 at Pebble and Mark O'Meara, who had a 67 at Pebble.
O'Meara has won this tournament a record four times, leading Duval to comment: "The way Mark plays here, you almost have to say he's the front-runner."
In fourth place at 14 under par was Sweden's Jesper Parnevik, who shot a 67 at Spyglass Hill.

Tiger Woods, who missed a 12-foot birdie putt on the 18th at Pebble Beach that would have equalled Duval's 62, was in fifth place at 11 under par along with three others after his nine-under round of 63.

The first three rounds of the tournament are played in two-man pro-am teams on three courses: Pebble, Spyglass, and Poppy Hills. In the final round the top 60 pros and top 25 pro-am teams compete on Pebble Beach.

Duval began his round with some exceptional iron shots. He was eight under par for the first seven holes, having knocked in four birdie putts of eight feet and under, as well as eagle putts of eight inches and six feet.
"I never really had to make a putt because I just kept hitting it so close," said Duval.
"It was so low, I thought it was a team score," said Woods about seeing Duval's score go up on the leaderboard.
Duval's pace slowed down considerably on the back nine. He had six birdie chances inside of 12 feet, but made just two of the putts.
Said Duval about his 62: "It's great whenever you can share a course record with a player like Tom Kite, but it's not as important as getting back into the tournament."
Duval, 26, is still looking for his first PGA Tour victory, having finished second five times, including here at Pebble Beach two years ago when Jacobsen won.

Last week at the Phoenix Open, Duval went into the final round in second place, but shot a final-round 78 to finish 14th. "I'm not the type of person who gets real high or low about the way I play," said Duval. "I held my head high after Phoenix because I did the best I could do that day."
Woods was able to shoot his best round of the week in part because he had become more adjusted to the huge crowds which followed him and his partner, actor Kevin Costner.
This tournament is the only one on the PGA Tour where, because of all the celebrity amateurs, spectators are allowed to use cameras.

"I don't mind the crowds," said Woods, "and I don't mind the fact that they take pictures, but they keep taking them while we're swinging, which is wrong. I got clicked pretty badly. Then you have a tough time putting because the green is lit up with flashes. It can get ridiculous.""
